I really, really like this.

I get why it's not to everyone's taste, but I found this so eerie and sad and beautiful at the same time, especially when she says she wants to have children, that line is just so freakin' tragic.

She's a ghost who doesn't know she's dead, and I have a feeling that her death was really horrible, which is why she's blocking out the memory of it. She was probably murdered in the house where she was found; in fact, I have it in my headcanon that all of this took place in L.A., and that she's Elizabeth Short, a.k.a. the Black Dahlia. :'(

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Something funny in the precautions…

If 126 has no physical form, why is caution needed to 'prevent physical contact'?

How would you even go about avoiding it? She's invisible and intangible, she could be *inside* somebody when they open her door to leave the room after a chat or something.

….For that matter, if she has no physical presence at all, how can she not go through solid objects? She doesn't exist as anything but a disembodied consciousness.

I do like the concept, but it needs clarification plot hole repair.
